title: Flat twisted Koszul chain pairing for lattice algebras
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $r\geq0$, and put $D=\mathbf Z^r$, $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal A_R(D)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $t:\mathcal M\to\mathcal E$ for trivial action and $\Gamma$ for invariants [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Use ordinary derived categories and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For equivariant cochain complexes use the finite Koszul complex of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] and its total $K(P)^n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}K_R(P^b;T)^a$, with differential $d_K+(-1)^a d_P$. Let $B$ be an internal commutative unital $R$-algebra with commuting $R$-algebra automorphisms $T_1,\ldots,T_r$, and put $K_B=K_R(B;T)$. Assume $B\otimes_R-$ is exact on $\mathcal M$. Then $K_B$ and $tK_B$ are flat-term K-flat bounded complexes in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal E$ respectively: total tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic. Put $T_A=\prod_{i\in A}T_i$ and $\epsilon(A,C)=(-1)^{\#\{(a,c)\in A\times C:c<a\}}$. The formula
$$(x\star y)_I=\sum_{A\sqcup C=I,\ |A|=p}\epsilon(A,C)x_A T_A(y_C)\qquad(x\in K_B^p,\ y\in K_B^q,\ |I|=p+q)$$
defines an internal $R$-bilinear chain map $\star:K_B\otimes_R K_B\to K_B$ with
$$d(x\star y)=dx\star y+(-1)^p x\star dy.$$
The degree-zero element $1_B$ gives a chain map $u:R[0]\to K_B$ and is a two-sided unit for $\star$. Ordinary tensors of these K-flat complexes represent their derived tensors. The assertions and formulas hold for $r=0$, the zero algebra, the zero ring and characteristic two; no assumption on $R$ beyond commutativity is imposed.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to regard internal modules as module sheaves on the small coherent profinite site. The relative tensor is the sheafification of the sectionwise balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: its universal balanced maps give the same internal relative tensor. By [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], $K_B^a$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $B$, zero outside $0\leq a\leq r$. Tensor with this sum is the finite direct sum of the exact functor $B\otimes_R-$. Thus every term is flat, including the zero terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] on this ringed site to the flat complex $K_B$, bounded above by $r$. It is K-flat in the acyclic-total-tensor sense [def-pc-kflat-complex]. In particular $\operatorname{Tot}(K_B\otimes_R A)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $A$; symmetry exchanges the two tensor factors with sign $(-1)^{ab}$ on bidegree $(a,b)$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, applied to the coherent profinite ringed site.

proof.text:
Let $U:\mathcal E\to\mathcal M$ forget the action. Its exactness and detection of exactness are [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]; its underlying diagonal tensor comparison is [def-sfb-condensed-action-tensor]. For a short exact sequence in $\mathcal E$, tensor with $tK_B^a$ becomes, under $U$, tensor with $K_B^a$ of the underlying short exact sequence, hence is exact. So $tK_B$ has flat terms and the same bounds. For any acyclic complex $A$ in $\mathcal E$, exactness gives acyclic $UA$, and
$$U\operatorname{Tot}(tK_B\otimes_R A)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(K_B\otimes_R UA).$$
This is the canonical chain isomorphism induced by the strong tensor comparison and the additive forgetful functor; it uses only finite sums in each degree, since $K_B$ is bounded. The right side is acyclic by Step 2; detection of exactness implies acyclicity on the left before forgetting. This proves K-flatness in $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), discrete-lattice input below the ordinary-open direct-image argument; explicit agent calculation.

proof.text: For disjoint $A,C$, the rule $(x,y)\mapsto xT_A(y)$ is $R$-balanced and additive in each variable because every $T_i$ is an internal $R$-algebra automorphism. It commutes with restrictions on the site, hence induces a map of sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Add these maps with coefficients $\epsilon(A,C)$ over the finite ordered partitions of $I$. This gives an internal degree-preserving bilinear map on $K_B\otimes_R K_B$, zero in impossible degrees. We check its differential against the explicit Koszul differential of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] in the next step.

source.place: Paragraph (3), discrete-lattice input below the ordinary-open direct-image argument; explicit agent calculation.

proof.text:
Fix homogeneous degrees $p,q\geq0$ and a target set $J$ of size $p+q+1$. Index terms by $J=A\sqcup C\sqcup\{i\}$, with $|A|=p$, $|C|=q$. Put $N=\#\{(a,c)\in A\times C:c<a\}$, $a=\#\{j\in A:j<i\}$ and $c=\#\{j\in C:j<i\}$. The contribution to $d(x\star y)_J$ has sign $(-1)^{N+a+c}$ and value
$$(T_i-1)(x_A T_A y_C)=T_i(x_A)T_AT_i(y_C)-x_AT_A(y_C).$$
In $(dx\star y)_J$, partition $J=(A\cup\{i\})\sqcup C$; the sign exponent is $(N+c)+a$. Its value is $(T_ix_A-x_A)T_AT_i(y_C)$. In $(-1)^p(x\star dy)_J$, partition $J=A\sqcup(C\cup\{i\})$; the exponent is $p+(N+p-a)+c$, congruent to $N+a+c$ modulo two. Its value is $x_AT_A(T_iy_C-y_C)$. Adding these last two values cancels $-x_AT_AT_i(y_C)$ with $+x_AT_AT_i(y_C)$ and gives the first displayed value. These indexings exhaust all summands, so summing proves the Leibniz identity. Only multiplicativity of $T_i$, commutation with $T_A$, and the stated differential [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] were used. The identity on generalized pure tensors gives equality of the internal morphisms by the tensor presentation [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus $\star$ is a chain map.

source.place: Paragraph (3), discrete-lattice input below the ordinary-open direct-image argument; explicit agent calculation.

proof.text: Every $T_i$ fixes $1_B$, so $d(1_B)=((T_i-1)1_B)_i=0$ by [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution]. The algebra unit $R\to B=K_B^0$, zero in other degrees, therefore defines $u:R[0]\to K_B$. For $u\star x$ the only partition has $A=\varnothing$, sign $+1$, and $T_A=1$. For $x\star u$ it has $C=\varnothing$, sign $+1$, and $T_A(1_B)=1_B$. Thus both products equal $x$. For $r=0$ the formulas reduce to ordinary multiplication and unit on $B[0]$. If $B$ or $R$ is zero all maps are the unique zero maps (and the identity of the zero object is zero); in characteristic two the same integral sign identities reduce modulo two. No division, nonzero hypothesis or restriction on characteristic was used.

proof.text: In $\mathcal M$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] applied to the flat-term K-flat complexes just established identifies their ordinary total tensors with their derived tensors. For the action category use its ordinary K-flat derived tensor as specified in [def-sfb-condensed-derived-cup]: the identity of $tK_B$ is already a flat-term K-flat replacement, by Step 3, so the defining representative formula computes its derived tensor by its ordinary total tensor. The same applies to $R[0]$ and $tR[0]$: tensoring with the regular unit is the identity, so these are flat and K-flat. This supplies all ordinary-to-derived tensor identifications asserted in the item.
